query: If the most common operational burdens described in the text were eliminated, how much would resolution duration drop?

per_column.name: primary_issue_category
per_column.rationale: Extracts a clear issue type from short_description, directly enabling grouping by 'most common operational burdens' central to the query. Values (wifi, vpn, database, printer) match source text soundly.

per_column.name: issue_scope
per_column.rationale: Scope (system-wide vs individual) is a useful axis for burden analysis, but the short descriptions rarely state scope. Labeling 'Cannot connect to office WiFi' or a single VPN failure as 'system_wide' is an unwarranted confident inference; the dominance of system_wide (362) suggests over-assertion.

per_column.name: technical_complexity
per_column.rationale: Complexity could correlate with resolution duration, giving analytical leverage. However it is a heuristic inference from category rather than something the text states; defensible as a categorisation but partly speculative.

per_column.name: issue_recurrence_pattern
per_column.rationale: Recurrence directly relates to 'operational burdens' and is analytically relevant. But the source text (single short descriptions with one timestamp) does not support daily/weekly/rare labels; assigning 'recurring_weekly' or 'recurring_daily' to isolated tickets is largely invented, contradicting available evidence.

per_column.name: assignee_resolution_efficiency
per_column.rationale: A resolution-efficiency axis is relevant to duration, but a binary high/moderate closure-rate label per row is not derivable from the shown fields (closed_by name alone). It appears to be an unsupported inference and is near-binary, limiting leverage.

per_column.name: assigned_technician_continuity
per_column.rationale: A true/false continuity flag adds little clear analytical leverage for the duration query, and its basis is unclear from the available columns; the per-row values are not evidently grounded and read as guessed.

judge.rationale: primary_issue_category is strong and directly serves the query's focus on common burdens. Several other columns (issue_scope, issue_recurrence_pattern, assignee_resolution_efficiency, technical_complexity) target relevant axes but assert categories the short single-ticket text does not support, producing confident specifics (system_wide, recurring_weekly/daily, closure-rate labels) that are not grounded. Groundedness is the main weakness across the set.
